# Analysis reproduction repository for "Low-frequency spectra of neutron star + OB supergiant binaries: Does wind density drive persistent and flaring modes of accretion?"

![Main result](main.png?raw=true "Lmm vs EW")

## Based on Van den Eijnden et al., MNRAS, 543, 862 (2025)
The full paper, included updated versions can be found on https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.04375 and https://academic.oup.com/mnras/article/543/1/862/8252964?login=true (open access).

This reproduction repository contains the following contents to reproduce the analysis and figures from the paper:
- the DATA folder contains the reduced data products and scripts used to analyse the millimeter images
- the FIGURES_and_ANALYSIS folder contains Jupyter notebooks to reproduce all calculations, fits, and plotting from the paper. It also contains the necessary input files for these calculations and plots.
- the PAPER folder contains manuscript pdf file and its TeX source files.

We refer to the full paper for justifications and explanations of all steps and decisions in this reproduction package, 

Note that, due to their file size, the reduced ALMA images are included as .zip files. Please extract these folders first, before running the measurements.py script inside CASA to measure the ALMA flux densities. 

Similarly, the calibrated measurement sets for the ALMA data, used in the variability analysis, are not included. The ALMA data is public and calibrated measurement sets can be requested via the CalMS service (https://almascience.eso.org/tools/eu-arc-network/the-european-arc-calms-service) and the MOUS UID from the ALMA archive. 

Please get in touch via email (jakobvandeneijnden.astro [at] gmail.com) or via github with questions.

If this repository is useful for your own research, in addition to citing the original paper, I request you add a note to this repository and/or its stable Zenodo DOI as well.

## Software requirements

The scripts in this reproduction package are written in python v3.12.8 and standard packages.
